The pacing of the story is exceptionally well-balanced and closely mirrors "real-time." The entire narrative spans roughly ten to fifteen minutes—starting at 6:40 AM and finishing safely before 7:00 AM—which takes only a few minutes to read. Rather than compressing large spans of time, the author stretches small, mundane moments through hyper-specific sensory details (a drop of water falling from a roof edge, testing a ballpoint pen, holding hot coffee in the mouth). This slight stretching of time effectively conveys the slow, rhythmic, and solitary nature of Ilse's routine on a foggy morning, while also building a quiet, atmospheric tension during the river crossing and the final moment when her phone rings.
